findings.title: Tar preflight can be desynchronised from tarfile via PAX size override, bypassing size limits
findings.message: preflight_tar sizes each member from the raw ustar header only. It never parses PAX records, so it ignores a PAX `size` override that tarfile honours. An attacker can put a PAX `size` before a file whose header says size 0. Preflight then reads that file's body as headers, hits an all-zero block, and returns early. tarfile still reads the whole body as one member, and parses any later `x`/`L` metadata header with a huge size by reading it fully into memory (`fileobj.read(self._block(self.size))`). The pre-parse bound on metadata and expanded size is therefore bypassable, which allows a memory or decompression DoS before the later per-member checks run. The 512 MiB in-memory compressed read does not mitigate this.
findings.suggestion: Make preflight match tarfile's framing. Either parse PAX records for `size` and `GNU.sparse.*` and apply the limits to the effective size, or reject any `x`/`g` header carrying a `size` key and any non-regular or sparse typeflag. Alternatively, iterate with tarfile using a bounded wrapper stream that caps decompressed bytes and metadata reads, and drop the separate re-implementation of the framing.

findings.title: Unsafe-member test passes for the wrong reason (generic ValueError)
findings.message: Each unsafe member is added to an archive whose manifest only covers the regular files. Every case therefore also fails with a coverage mismatch ValueError. The bare assertRaises(ValueError) passes even if traversal, symlink, hardlink, absolute-path and duplicate checks are missing or broken. Each case needs its own expected error.
findings.suggestion: Add the extra member's checksum to the manifest where applicable, and assert a specific message per case, for example assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'unsafe|link|duplicate|absolute'). The test should fail if only the coverage check is present.
